sources.note: Table of tone systems by Bantoid group gives for Jarawan: 'No analysis'. Text: 'Some families, such as Jarawan, lack a single reliable synchronic description of tone. However, if the evidence from North Bantoid is relevant, then early Bantoid probably had either two or three level tones, as well as rising and falling.' Nothing on Dulbu specifically; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. Jarawan Bantu: a new look at an orphan group. Slides presented at Bantoid II, Yaoundé, 7 June 2024. Department of Indigenous Affairs, Arunachal Pradesh / McDonald Institute for Archaeological Research, Cambridge / Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Academia.edu item 120641225 (7 figures; page text).
sources.note: No phonology of Dulbu. The Dulbu slide reads: 'we have definitive information on the death of Dulbu. Dulbu is/was spoken among the South Bauchi languages south of Bauchi town. An SIL team visited in 2019 and found no remaining speakers. The data collected by Shimizu will remain the only evidence. Though I still plan a revisit to check for rememberers. Dulbu ethnic identity remains very strong.' Elsewhere the deck notes pharyngealised/breathy vowels in some Jarawan lects and vowel counts for Jaku/Mbula; the only 'tone' hit is inside 'stone-walled'. Nothing on stress, accent or tone for Dulbu o…
